subject: RFP: commercial token economics & tiered overage scenarios
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@megacorp.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@megacorp.com
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: commercial questions - token pricing & commit structure

Connor —

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. We're compiling the commercial appendix for the MegaCorp RFP and have a few focused questions on token economics that we need clarified for procurement:

1) Please provide hosted API (on-demand) and committed pricing for text generation and embeddings expressed per 1K tokens and per token equivalence. Call out which models these buckets map to (e.g., curated base models vs. fine-tuned).

2) Define commit terms you support (monthly vs. annual, ramping, minimums) and how overages are charged (multipliers, rounding, billing granularity).

3) Provide two numerical scenarios we can include in the RFP appendix: (A) 1B tokens/month baseline with 12-month commit, (B) variable usage that spikes 3x for one month. Show invoicing math and effective $/1K token.

4) Are there differences for Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC/on‑prem) commercials we should expect in the pricing appendix? If so, summarize.

We need a short appendix we can attach to the RFP by EOD Thursday (2026-07-01). If you can send a worked example and a short commercial sheet, that would be ideal.

Thanks —
Jane Doe
Procurement Manager
MegaCorp Inc.

Attachment: None
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RFP: commercial questions - token pricing & commit structure

Jane —

Appreciate the clarity — attaching a concise commercial sheet and a worked spreadsheet with scenario math. High level answers below; the attachment (redwood-commercial-sheet-v1.pdf) has the same language you can drop into the RFP.

Summary (short):
- On-demand (hosted API): billed per 1K tokens; no minimum. Generation: $0.20 / 1K tokens. Embeddings: $0.08 / 1K tokens.
- Committed (annual or 12-month monthly commit): volume discount applied to on-demand list; typical committed rate shown below (12-month example). Overage charges billed at 1.25x the committed rate, billed in 1K-token increments.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): priced as a mix of fixed monthly capacity + reduced per-1K token for sustained throughput; provides lower latency and predictable SLOs. Private (VPC/on-prem): platform fee + installation/ops fee; per-token economics are negotiated separate from hosted catalogs.

Key commercial bullets:
- Commit terms supported: 3, 6, 12, 24 month. Minimums: none for hosted on-demand; committed stacks start at 0.5B tokens/month.
- Overage policy: monthly true-up; any usage beyond committed units in a billing period charged at 125% of committed rate (rounded to nearest 1K token).
- Pricing locks: committed rates are guaranteed for the term; model upgrades within equivalent capability buckets do not change price.

Attached: redwood-commercial-sheet-v1.pdf (concise appendix), pricing-scenarios-appendix.xlsx (worksheets with math).

I'll send worked scenarios inline next to make it easy to paste.

Thanks —
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

Connor —

Helpful — thank you. A couple of clarifying points before you finalize the appendix:  

- Can you show the effective $/1K token after discounts and over three sample months (steady, +1 month spike, and 3x sustained)? Procurement will want to see effective blended price.
- How does embedding consumption factor into the commit? Is that counted against the same commit bucket or a separate SKU?
- Please confirm billing granularity (do you bill per-request, per-minute, or per-1K-token buckets) and whether there is a prorated true-up if a customer increases a commit mid-term.

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@megacorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: commercial questions - token pricing & commit structure

Jane —

Below are the detailed worked scenarios and answers to each of your clarifying points. Please use the table text verbatim in the RFP appendix if useful. If Legal wants a formal commercial appendix in PDF we can finalize in DocuSign after you confirm.

Pricing buckets (for RFP appendix):
- On-demand (hosted API): Generation $0.20 / 1K tokens; Embeddings $0.08 / 1K tokens.
- Committed (12-month example, monthly billed): Generation $0.14 / 1K tokens (30% discount off on-demand); Embeddings $0.056 / 1K tokens (30% discount).
- Overage: 125% of committed rate (i.e., 1.25 x committed).
- Billing granularity: 1K-token buckets; usage rounded up to nearest 1K per request.
- Commit inclusions: generation and embedding tokens are separate SKUs; customers can elect a blended commit that covers both (requires explicit split in contract) or purchase separate commits. Standard RFP assumes separate SKUs for clarity.
- Mid-term changes: increases in commit are prorated for the remainder of the term and effective immediately; decreases are applied at the next renewal (no retroactive refunds).
- Invoice cadence: monthly invoicing with line-item true-up; overage charges appear on the invoice for the month they occurred. If an invoice overcharges relative to contract terms, credits are issued on the next invoice cycle after reconciliation.

Worked scenarios (paste-friendly):

Scenario A — Steady baseline (1,000,000,000 tokens / month generation):
- On-demand cost: 1,000,000,000 tokens / 1,000 * $0.20 = $200,000.00 per month.
- Committed (12-month @ $0.14 / 1K): 1,000,000,000 / 1,000 * $0.14 = $140,000.00 per month.
- Effective $/1K tokens: $140.00 / 1,000 = $0.14 / 1K (committed).
- If usage hits exactly the commit, no overage.

Scenario B — Single-month 3x spike (month 6 usage = 3B tokens, commit still 1B):
- Committed coverage: first 1B charged at committed rate = $140,000.00.
- Overage: additional 2B tokens charged at 1.25 x $0.14 = $0.175 / 1K. Overage cost = 2,000,000,000 / 1,000 * $0.175 = $350,000.00.
- Month 6 invoice total = $140,000 + $350,000 = $490,000.00.
- Effective blended $/1K for month 6 = $490,000 / (3,000,000 * 1) = $0.1633 per 1K tokens (i.e., $163.33 / 1M tokens).

Scenario C — Sustained 3x (3B tokens/mo sustained for 3 months) and option to increase commit mid-term to 3B:
Option 1 — pay overages for the three months: each month charged as in Scenario B ($490,000 per month). Three-month total = $1,470,000.
Option 2 — increase commit to 3B/month (prorated for remainder of term). Example prorate math (month 2 of 12 remain = 11 months left):
- New committed rate still $0.14 / 1K (example pricing) and prorated commitment charge to scale baseline billed as part of monthly invoice; operationally we calculate the incremental committed spend and apply moving forward. Net effective $/1K after commit increase would be $0.14 / 1K for covered volume; overage would then be charged only if >3B.

Embeddings handling:
- Embeddings are a separate SKU by default. Example: if you purchase a 500M token embedding commit at $0.056 / 1K and generation commit at 1B tokens at $0.14 / 1K, they are invoiced and trued-up separately. If you prefer a single blended commit we can model that in the spreadsheet appendix; legal language must specify the split and how overages are allocated.

Other commercial notes:
- Rounding: we always round up usage to the next 1K token bucket.
- Credits: overage credits or billing corrections are posted on the next invoice after reconciliation (typically within one billing cycle).
- Marketplace/third-party fees: if you consume via a partner marketplace (cloud marketplace) there may be platform fees; direct Redwood billing avoids that layer.

If you'd like, we can produce two versions of the appendix: a short one-paragraph summary and a detailed table with line-item math. The attached spreadsheet contains the detailed lines (you can paste cells into the RFP).

I'll escalate to Pricing & Legal for a formal commercial appendix once you confirm the numbers you want included verbatim.

Best —
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com
